title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Roll Terms Carried by Each Marketing Programme
content:
Rolling is the moving out of a delivery period or a referenced futures month on Grain Marketing Contracts. What each programme allows, the smallest parcel it will roll and the administrative charge it carries per bushel rolled are catalogue terms of the programme.

| Programme | Administrative charge per bushel rolled (USD) | Rolls allowed in one crop year (count) | Smallest parcel a single instruction may roll (bushels) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 0.000 | 0 | 0 |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 0.030 | 2 | 1000 |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 0.025 | 3 | 5000 |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 0.040 | 4 | 5000 |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 0.000 | 0 | 0 |
| Minimum Price Contract | 0.040 | 2 | 5000 |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 0.035 | 6 | 10000 |

A programme carrying a roll ceiling of 0 rolls nothing at all: neither the Spot Cash Delivery Ticket nor the Delayed Price Agreement is rolled, and the charge and the parcel size are accordingly nil on both.

## The count read at the boundary

The roll ceiling is a count for one crop year on one contract. A Hedge-to-Arrive Contract that has taken four rolls in the crop year has reached its ceiling; a Basis Fixed Contract that has taken two has one left in the year. The smallest parcel is the least a single instruction may name: on the Managed Accumulator Program an instruction stands for at least 10,000 bushels, and on the Forward Cash Sale Contract for at least 1,000.
